data.title: BB Stock Rises Overnight: BlackBerry Takes On Browser Security With New Windows Launch Amid US Tech Outage
data.description:
Key points:
  • BlackBerry launched its Chromium-based secure browser for Windows, extending its mobile offering to desktops. 
  • It lets users access work apps like Outlook, Teams, and OneDrive on personal computers. 
  • U.S. intelligence chief Jay Clayton warned of more technology outages as organizations upgrade systems. 

BlackBerry (BB) stock rose overnight as the company said its secure Windows browser helps businesses protect work data without managing employees’ personal computers. The launch comes as U.S. intelligence chief Jay Clayton warns that technology upgrades could lead to more outages across critical systems.

BlackBerry stock traded over 3% higher overnight, ahead of Monday.

BlackBerry Bets On Workplace Applications And Secure Connectivity

On Friday, BlackBerry said its new Access Secure Browser for Windows uses Chromium technology to extend its enterprise security capabilities to desktop users. The launch builds on its existing iOS and Android offerings and replaces the previous desktop version.

This could make internal applications accessible from unmanaged Windows machines without needing companies to issue additional hardware. The Windows browser supports web applications, allowing services such as Outlook, Teams and OneDrive to operate in dedicated desktop windows.

BlackBerry Highlights Data Sovereignty Feature 

BlackBerry also highlighted the browser's deployment architecture as a selling point for government agencies, regulators and critical infrastructure operators. Many competing secure browsing products depend on cloud-based management systems operated by external vendors, raising concerns around jurisdiction and control.

BlackBerry Access operates within an encrypted BlackBerry Dynamics container and uses the BlackBerry Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) framework. Organizations running UEM on their own premises can retain browser administration, identity management, and security policies within their infrastructure.

BlackBerry’s Secure Communications division provides mission-critical software—including UEM, SecuSUITE encrypted voice and messaging, and AtHoc critical event management. In the second quarter, the division outperformed expectations, expanding 5 percentage points year-on-year to 66% and generating $9.7 million in adjusted EBITDA.

U.S. Intelligence Chief Warns Of More Tech Outages

BlackBerry’s update lands as U.S. intelligence chief Jay Clayton warned that technology outages could become more common as companies and government agencies upgrade older systems to improve performance and security.

A series of U.S. tech outages in November disrupted Microsoft services, air travel, major banks, and the National Security Agency. Most were caused by software errors, equipment failures, or efforts to upgrade old systems, not cyberattacks.

BB Stock: Retail Stance

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bearish’.

A user said, “Between QNX, Secure Communications, government and defense contracts, automotive technology and the growing opportunity in physical AI, BlackBerry has multiple avenues for growth that the market hasn’t fully priced in.”

Another user said, “The previous CEO was laughably incapable of monetizing every opportunity handed to him on silver platters. Let's see if the current CEO can capitalize on a nation security and market meltdown episode.”

BB stock has gained 105% year-to-date.

data.title: ABB to Buy Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22 Billion
data.description:
(06:01 GMT) *ABB to Buy Ziehl-Abegg
(06:02 GMT) *ABB to Buy Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22B
(06:02 GMT) *ABB: Deal Expands Offering for HVAC and Industrial Cooling Applications
(06:03 GMT) *ABB: Acquisition Adds Electronically Commutated Fans to Motion Portfolio
(06:04 GMT) *ABB: Intends to Retain Ziehl-Abegg's Headquarters in Kuenzelsau, Germany
(06:04 GMT) *ABB: Germany Will Remain an Important Location for the Business
(06:20 GMT) ABB to Buy Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22 Billion

By Adria Calatayud

ABB said it agreed to buy Ziehl-Abegg, a German manufacturer of fans, motors and ventilation systems, for $2.22 billion.

The Swiss engineering group said Monday that the deal expands its offering for heating, ventilation and air conditioning as well as industrial-cooling applications.

Ziehl-Abegg is expected to generate about $1.4 billion in revenue in 2026 and its products are used in HVAC, data centers, clean rooms, medical technology and elevator drives, among other uses.

The acquisition aims to add electronically commutated fans to the portfolio of motors and drives of ABB's Motion business, the company said. ABB said Ziehl-Abegg's profitability is expected to be in line with that of its own operations in the area within three years after closing of the transaction, which is anticipated in the second half of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.

ABB said it intends to retain Ziehl-Abegg's headquarters in Kuenzelsau, Germany, and that it will remain committed to the country.

data.title: Trump hosts meme coin dinner as token drops
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump, who has earned hundreds of millions of dollars from his $TRUMP meme coin, said at a dinner for the token’s top holders on Sunday that his support for the cryptocurrency was driven by a desire to strengthen the United States’ economic competitiveness.

“I’m doing it for the United States ... If we don’t do it, China’s going to do it,” Trump told attendees at his golf club outside Washington, according to reports. It was the third time Trump had held a gala for the top owners of his meme coin, which once soared as high as $75 ​but has fallen to a record low of under $1.

The gala’s access and perks are divided by tiers for the 185 holders of $TRUMP, the president’s meme coin. The top 29 investors are invited to a VIP reception, and the top four will receive a “TRUMP 18K Gold Watch”, according to the event’s website.

Attendees qualified for the dinner based on their time-weighted holdings of the $TRUMP ⁠coin from September 30 to November 16. Reports say organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets met the criteria for Sunday's dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just ​130 wallets when the contest concluded on November 16.

The May 2025 event's biggest $TRUMP holder was China-born crypto billionaire Justin Sun, who had $18.5M of the token. This time, there was no Sun at the event signing ​autographs, as per Reuters.

data.title: Anthropic Stock Trend, Jensen Huang’s Potential Return As Nvidia CEO And Dell’s Q4 Results To Keep Tech Investors Busy This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Investors will track ANT’s first-week run for valuation sustainability and potential read-throughs for other AI stocks. 
  • Dell’s report on Tuesday will test its record 2026 run, which eased since September.
  • Hewlett Packard, HP Inc. and Zoom also report earnings this week.

Investors will watch for developments around Jensen Huang’s potential return as Nvidia CEO, including reactions from the company's board and major shareholders following President Donald Trump's public backing.

Anthropic’s first week as a publicly traded company will also be in focus, with investors tracking its first few days of trading for signs of valuation sustainability and potential implications for other AI stocks.

The earnings calendar will add to the activity, with HP and Dell among the companies reporting results. U.S. markets will be closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Here are the top tech events to watch:

Tech IPOs

After a historic IPO, investors will be watching Anthropic stock (ANT) this week. Shares rose 17% on the opening day last Thursday but lost steam the next day. ANT stock and the broader tech market gained in the overnight trading ahead of Monday in what appeared to be a relief rally.

Tech Earnings

Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Zoom Communications (Nov. 23): As the earnings period draws to a close, the two reports would offer remaining insights into the demand for AI servers and enterprise software, respectively.

Analysts expect HPE’s fourth-quarter revenue to rise 49% to $14.43 billion and adjusted profit to more than double to $1.29 per share, according to Koyfin. They expect Zoom’s Q3 sales to rise 4% to $1.28 billion and EPS to drop 2% to $1.49 per share.

Dell Technologies and HP Inc. (Nov. 24): Tuesday will be crucial, as Dell’s report will test its record 2026 run, which has eased since September, while HP’s report takes on greater significance after Intel flagged sharp weakness in the personal computers market.

Analysts expect Dell’s Q3 revenue to rise 11% to $27.0 billion and adjusted profit to increase 20% to $2.59 per share. They expect HPQ’s Q4 revenue to rise 4.5% to $15.3 billion and adjusted profit to decrease 20% to $0.74 per share.

data.title: ABB to acquire Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.65 billion
data.description:
ABB said on Monday it would acquire German ventilation and drive technology maker Ziehl-Abegg for an enterprise value of $2.65 billion.

The Swiss engineering group said the deal valued Ziehl-Abegg at 1.9 times its expected 2026 sales and 18.6 times earning before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. ABB expects to close the acquisition in the second half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.
